sections.content:
Lectures:

Week 1: Introduction

Week 1, 2: Fundamental Concepts
Charge, current, voltage, circuit modeling, lumped parameter model, Ohm’s law, two-terminal element, reference direction, electric power, voltage and current sources, dependent sources, active
and passive elements

Week 2, 3, 4: DC Analysis
Circuit terminology, KCL, KVL, series/parallel connections, voltage/current dividers, nodal/mesh
analyses, linearity, superposition, Thevenin’s and Norton’s theorems, source transformation

Week 5, 6: Op Amp
Ideal op amp, voltage buffer, non-inverting amp, inverting amp, adder, difference amp, instrumentation amp, current source, negative impedance converter, V-to-I converter, ADC, DAC, differentiator, integrator

Week: 7, 8, 9: AC Analysis
Capacitor and inductor, sinusoidal excitation, steady-state and transient responses, complex number, phasor representation, magnitude and phase of steady-state response, impedance, AC power

Week: 10, 11: Frequency Response
Transfer function, poles and zeros, Bode plots, low-pass / band-pass / high-pass filters, first and second order systems

Week: 11, 12: Transient Analysis
Transient circuits, switch operations, RC and RL circuits, first order transient response

Week 13: Diode Circuits
Diode models, clipping and clamping circuits, half-wave and full-wave rectifiers, Zener diode, regulator, charge pump
---

Labs:

Lab 1a/b: Instrumentation and Measurement
Lab 2: PSpice Circuit Simulation (can use LTSpice)
Lab 3: Light-Tracking Car (Digital Control)
Lab 4: Light-Tracking Car (Analog Control)
Lab 5a: Audio Equalizer (PSpice Simulation) (can use LTSpice)
Lab 5b:  Audio Equalizer

sections.content:
Before i am going to talk about the contents in this course, i suggested every students who enrolled ELEC1100 and PHYS1114 should go through DC analysis in this course first. Why? because the node analysis and some DC techniques are super important for you to deal with some DC circult .For example,PHYS1114 and ELEC1100 midterm have some questions to find voltage/resistors/current.With DC analysis techniques,it is trivial for you to KO these kinds of questions in just 10-30 seconds.

OK about the contents (i will rate the importance from 1-10):
CH1 (1): review from ELEC1100(recall the memory from high school physics)
CH2 (10): DC analysis,including KCL,KVL ,node analysis,dependent sources,power, Thevenin and Norton
You should know all this kinds of questions very well because the method in dealing AC analysis in this course is very similar to DC analysis, so please take some times to make sure you really understand these concepts.
CH3 (6): OP-amp :Ideal op amp, voltage buffer, non-inverting amp, inverting amp, adder, difference amp, instrumentation amp
Quite easy,you can just memorize i- = i+ = 0 and v- = v+ if you are really lazy. One thing need to remind ,you should understand about negative and positive feedback(schmitt trigger) cuz they are acting different purposes and different behaviors

CH4 (6): AC analysis: Capacitor and inductor, sinusoidal excitation, steady-state and transient responses, complex number, phasor representation
Not hard also because you guys no need to calculate with ODE,instead,this courses use laplace transform to change the time domain to frequency domain for easy calculations.
You guys need to understand complex number quite well (phase and magnitude) and i will discuss this part in workload part(have some tips in exam)

CH5 (5) :Frequency Response :bode plot etc... still you need to understand complex number quite well to deal with laplace element(zeros and poles).It's ok for you guys to just memorize the method which taught in tutorial

CH6 (7):Transient Analysis :RC/RL circult. Basically it is just a ODE equation but no need to solve ODE,Instead we just memorize the equation given in lectures.I think this one is quite a little bit challenging because you have to think carefully when the timing is 0- 0+ and inf...

CH7 (9): Diode :dlode model ,zener diode etc...The keys concept in this thing is-----just a guess.Yes i am not joking,you have to guess which diode is on and off so that the circult perform in a correct http://way.It might be confusing cuz it is quite abstract to think about which guess is correct .
(p.s. if you wanna go further study in ELEC3400 3500,you have to get familiar with diode cuz BJT and mosfet will be taught(which actually is diode) )

However, i think this course is quite easy and didn't cover some methods (like introduction in BJT,how to design the circult etc...)
So in general i will rate content in B

内容安排算是合理的，其实别人也说差不多了我觉得大家必须好好学的东西也就几个重要的点吧（因为我自己mid错了很多这种玩意所以喜提mid一般的分）

0. 基础 为啥我说基础，因为你要搞明白定义（node是什么？/为什么短路了就会像短路那样？提示：很明显你可以自己拿1/Req=1/R1+1/0来算算R应该是什么鬼，这点ricky会教/把电压/电流杀了之后是啥样的（自己想想V=0/I=0是啥就行了）不然你做题就是会懵逼

1. KCL 这个课mid/final就是花样kcl，说难听点你一上来最好就把kvl什么的垃圾定律忘掉（因为没kcl简单）那么kcl的精髓是什么呢？相当于你要会看node（这一点是很难的，要搞明白定义啊！node本质上是等压的一个区域，可以是一个点，也可以是等压的一大条线！）知道了node，你就开始ohm’s law，把几个东西变成V/R的表达式就秒了！要找到电工测点电压那种感觉！

2. Thevenin 学懂这个和开路/短路的定义就行了，不要傻乎乎看着俩没连个环的线还在想电压啥样废话肯定是等电压的！norton本质也不太用在意因为他可以被Vth/Req算出来 Superposition（这个自己学就行）

3. Op-Amp 你确实可以无脑I+=I-=0，但是自己看看V+/V-需要什么前置条件

4. Frequency Domain 哎这玩意和2100一样的，本质上什么impedance啊ac的current啊voltage就是fix一个频率把东西傅立叶变换成只在那个频率非0的basis（意思就是omega是200的时候，你那堆V啊I的东西就是他的amplitude或者自己三角函数拆了搞个phase diff）没啥难的地方，注意一下一些元件的arg其实不一样的就行了；其次就是自己多好好听听ricky怎么教bode plot的 很受用

5. Transient 注意一下啥东西应该连续（capacitor的V etc）然后我们不cover RLC 爽了

6. Diode 就是猜，你以为还有什么技巧？？

Note: please take this review with a grain of salt. I wrote this review to get access to class reviews since I am exchange student here for 1 semester. So I will just write a quick review about the equivalent of this class at my university and maybe leave some tips about taking the class from a course material perspective.

Basic circuit analysis will not be difficult. It starts out similar to the circuit analysis you are introduced to during a physics electromagnetic course. To be successful at circuit analysis it is crucial to understand nodes to see whether circuit components are series or parallel. Thevenin and Norton equivalents are easy concepts to understand if you have the fundamental analysis understood.

The real challenge in any electronic circuits course is the introduction to the ac analysis and the use of complex numbers or phasor format. Possibly look towards outside class resources to get a better understanding of what phasors mean as they are very important in later classes such as power electronics and signals and systems. Another challenging aspect of circuit analysis if this class goes into will be higher order circuits. This may require an understanding of solving ordinary differential equations and possibly using a laplace transform.

Much of electrical engineering circuit analysis will come back to the fundamentals learned in this course.
sections.teaching: I cannot really comment on the teaching in this course. However I believe doing circuit analysis example problems will be the best way to learn the material. Especially circuits that are more complex and not intuitive to understand. Having a professor explain the method of circuit analysis helps a lot in developing your own method of approaching circuit analysis.
sections.grading:
At my home university it was absolute grading. However since this class is notorious for being a weed out course the grade averages are quite low on exams so usually people are bumped up by 5-10 points to the final grade in any given semester. Exam grades median in the low 70s.
Grading Scale:
A 90-100
B 80-89
C 70-79
D 60-69
F <60
sections.workload: Workload in this class for me at least was not too bad. If I practiced enough circuits eventually it became quite intuitive to my understanding. If you can get to a level of intuitive understanding of circuit analysis I believe the workload of this course will be easily manageable. For labs if it is breadboard circuit building it is quite crucial to ensure that the nodes you are building follow the diagram or given design specifications. Sometimes if you are stuck it helps to double check the connections. Once I spent an additional 2 hours in a lab because my connections were not correctly orientated

In general, get yourself a crew if you are going to take this course. I will further explain down below.

1. Homework: Start working on your assignments right at their release

- Questions are normal to hard difficulty, that's why you have to team up and solve the problems together. Struggling with homework together can give you the feeling that you are not alone, hence reducing stress.

- You are usually given 2 weeks to complete them. sections.content:
1. Introduction (Basic concepts such as voltage, current, power, etc.)
2. DC analysis
3. AC analysis
4. Operation amplifier (opamp)
5. Frequency response
6. Transient analysis
7. Diode

Basically, the whole course is again teaching you how to calculate voltage and current from looking at a circuit diagram, but with some new circuit components (opamp, diode, etc.) or concepts (transient analysis). However, those concept are not very difficult at all. Even though you got lost in ELEC1100, you can catch up here if you work hard. Moreover, the difficulties are not as horrible as PHYS1114 so don't afraid even though you screw up that.

Better remember KCL and KVL by heart and master them because no matter what new concepts or components are added, you will use these two things always. When you see a "T" crossroads or "+" crossroads in the circuit diagram, applying KCL at there always helps you to proceed.

I think the most challenging part of this course is not the content. Instead, it is the lack of confidence on your answers. It is not uncommon to encounter a situation that even yourself are doubted on your own answers, especially when you see a lot of ugly numbers or lengthy expression. When you are checking answers with others, you will discover that 10 people will have 10 different answers and you will become afraid. Therefore, try to put more confidence so that you can do exams calmly and won't freak out. That may rather give you better result.

Another thing is CAREFULNESS. Since the topic is not really hard, you may become less alerted. Here are some examples (DON'T do them)
1. Overlook / Reverted a +ve / -ve sign (very often and severe for students)
2. Overlook 5k as 5
3. 1/(10i) = -10i (i = imaginary number)

Please pay extremely attention when you are solving questions, ESPECIALLY THE +VE / -VE SIGN. For this course, the +ve / -ve sign is even more fatal than the number itself. Careless mistakes may cost you one subgrade.
